practice1.hint: matplotlib is not installed here, so this exercise reads your code instead of drawing anything. Write what you would run on your own machine, including the parts that make the picture readable to somebody who did not write it.

questions.prompt: What is the conventional import for matplotlib's plotting interface?
questions.explain: Almost every example you will read online uses plt, so following the convention makes other people's code readable to you and yours to them.

choices: Saves the figure to a file
Displays the figure that the earlier calls built up
questions.explain: The plot, label and title calls all add to a figure that is being assembled. show() is the point where it is put on screen.

questions.prompt: Match each plot type to the question it answers best.
right: How are these values spread out?
How does this change over time?
Do these two variables move together?
questions.explain: Picking the wrong type does not fail; it just answers a question nobody asked. The shape of the data decides the shape of the chart.

questions.prompt: Put the steps of building a simple plot in order.
questions.explain: Everything before show() adds to the same figure. Calling show() first would display an empty one.

questions.prompt: Which of these change how a line is drawn?
questions.explain: bins belongs to a histogram: it decides how the values are grouped, not how a line looks.
